scope: Resource content hash removal; explicit IDs/versions, actual structure and frame identity remain
compatibility: Existing v2 SQLite uses immediate transactions to add explicit revision/bundle references and migration mapping tables; original columns, snapshot JSON, point BLOB, raw JSON and ACK values are retained.

Legacy snapshot association uses actual recipe ID/version and actual structures, never legacy digest values. Missing or ambiguous snapshots leave history readable but cannot reproduce or fall back to the current recipe.
Corrective migration does not trust previous synthetic snapshots as legacy sources; new explicit runtime records remain intact.
Old publication directories are read through stable randomly assigned legacy-bundle IDs and a persisted directory-locator mapping. Directories and old manifests are not renamed or rewritten.
Retired recipe versions survive delete, rename and restart. Historical version floors are loaded before automatic samples, and failed publication writes do not consume the frozen target version.

New raw references persist recorded width/height. Legacy references use matching cycle/view/file metadata when present; decoded dimension changes and malformed metadata are refused without content hashes.
PLC DBD20/84 and all other offsets remain fixed; reserved words must be zero. No plan content digest is computed or compared.
Real temporary Windows junctions between cycles and linked roots are rejected before canonicalization and on later reads.
Missing/zero legacy recipe versions normalize to one; subsequent saves use the actual monotonic version floor.
